clue.text: A legitimate target for blonde with grouse, say

parts.note: blonde hair is described as fair
grouse is an example of game, birds shot for sport

explanation.surface: Someone thinks a fair-haired person who complains a lot deserves to be picked on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grouse' looks like a verb meaning complain; with 'say' it is the bird, an example of game.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a person or thing that may justly be attacked or criticised.

clue.text: Rue changes following a saucy opening

indicators.note: following says the next letters come after those built so far

parts.note: saucy, in the sense of cheeky, means pert

indicators.note: changes tells us the letters of the word rue are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone regrets a cheeky first remark they made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rue' looks like regret but is just fodder; 'changes' makes URE, and 'following' puts it after the saucy part.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a hole or gap through which light or air passes.

clue.text: Protested over trade terms? No

indicators.note: over, as in turned over, tells us the letters of the following words are tossed about

explanation.surface: A negotiator questions the terms of a deal and turns them down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is the anagram signal: the twelve letters of TRADE TERMS plus NO are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to object forcefully or argue against something.

clue.text: A drug smuggler needs time and charm

parts.note: a mule is slang for someone carrying drugs across a border

explanation.surface: A courier of narcotics relies on timing and personal charisma.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charm' looks like personal appeal but is the lucky trinket.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a trinket worn to ward off evil or bring luck.

clue.text: A point for the animal that doesn't start

indicators.note: something that doesn't start has lost its opening letter, so the first letter of the word goes

parts.note: a beast is an animal

explanation.surface: Someone argues that a sluggish creature deserves a mark in its favour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doesn't start' removes B, the first letter of BEAST.
explanation.definitionFit: A compass point, one of the four cardinal directions.

clue.text: How to get rid of wrinkles, and reduce…

definitions.text: How to get rid of wrinkles

explanation.surface: Advice on smoothing out creases, whether in fabric or the face, runs on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition reads the answer as DE-CREASE, removing a crease; the ellipsis joins the surface to 7-down.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking creases out is a whimsical reading of the word; it also plainly means to make smaller or lessen.

clue.text: …part of the problem in ironing dress

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Smoothing creases is a problem when ironing a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A mini is a short dress or skirt, from miniskirt or minidress.

clue.text: Overwhelm one sister on an assignation

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, says the next piece sits after what comes before it

parts.note: the Roman numeral I stands for one
a nun is a religious sister
an assignation is a date, a romantic meeting

explanation.surface: A nun goes out on a romantic rendezvous and finds it all too much.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to flood or swamp with more than can be dealt with.

clue.text: Hate to find a different interpretation

parts.note: a version is a particular, different interpretation or account

explanation.surface: Someone resents having to come up with yet another reading of events.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a strong dislike or disinclination.

clue.text: Call for prison sentence

explanation.surface: A judge pronounces how long someone must spend inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To term something is to name or call it; a term is also the length of a sentence served in jail.

clue.text: The removal of oil to Iran — bet it goes astray!

indicators.note: anything that goes astray wanders off course, so these letters are scrambled into a new order

explanation.surface: A gambler bets on oil being shipped off to Iran, and the deal goes wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes astray' rearranges the twelve letters of OIL TO IRAN and BET; 'it' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: complete destruction or wiping out, so that nothing remains.

clue.text: Court official supporting measure for aid to reproduction

indicators.note: supporting, in a down clue, puts the second piece underneath the first

parts.note: a tape is a tape measure
a recorder is a judge in certain English courts

explanation.surface: A court officer stands below a ruler, helping to replicate something.
explanation.walkthrough: A recorder is a part-time judge in English courts; 'reproduction' means reproducing sound, not breeding.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine for playing back sound is a device that helps with reproducing audio.

clue.text: A source of thiamin in peas and beans beats…

indicators.note: in tells us the letters go inside the following word

parts.note: peas and beans are pulses, edible seeds of legumes

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it begins, so only its opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: A nutritionist notes that legumes provide vitamin B1, and the text runs on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: A and T (first letter of thiamin) go inside PULSES.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: throbs rhythmically, as a heart does.

clue.text: Abolish bushes

explanation.surface: Someone decides to get rid of the shrubbery altogether.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrub a plan is to cancel it; scrub is also low stunted vegetation.

clue.text: …a cold in Swiss mountain — a beast

indicators.note: in here means placed in position after, so the next letters come next

parts.note: an alp is a mountain in Switzerland
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone catches a chill up in the Alps, which sounds beastly.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces sit side by side: ALP, then A and C, then the second A.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a South American animal related to the llama, kept for wool.

clue.text: There are some hiding in the end

indicators.note: some hiding in says a few letters lie concealed inside the words before

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people are holed up at the very back.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'hiding in the end' as the definition, but that cannot stand in for the answer; 'some hiding in' signals the run inside THERE ARE, and 'the end' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: the back part, as in bringing up the rear.

clue.text: Crack, withholding call up, and is not forthcoming

indicators.note: withholding means holding something inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a rent is a split or tear

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, says the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to cite is to call, as a witness

explanation.surface: A safe-cracker refuses to call anyone and keeps quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' is the split, not a verb; 'up' turns the call word into ETIC, held inside by 'withholding'; 'and is' are links, so the definition is an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: reserved, unwilling to reveal much.

clue.text: Good to be found in empty boat

indicators.note: to be found in says one piece is located inside another

parts.note: bare means empty, as in bare shelves

explanation.surface: Something good is discovered aboard an abandoned vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a flat-bottomed boat used on canals and rivers.

clue.text: A common look for a shop

explanation.surface: A shopper takes a quick glance at a store.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang, butcher's hook means look, shortened to butcher's; 'common' signals the slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a butcher's is slang for a glance; the trade name also denotes a meat retailer's premises.

clue.text: Hurry up, people!

explanation.surface: An urgent shout telling everyone to get a move on.
explanation.definitionFit: To race is to hurry; a race is also a people of common descent.

clue.text: Poorly directed but given a mention

indicators.note: poorly means badly done, so these letters are put in a wrong order

explanation.surface: A badly directed film still got a nod from the critics.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: acknowledged or named as responsible, as in a film's closing roll.

clue.text: A mild rebuke, however viewed

indicators.note: however viewed says the letters read the same from either direction

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Disapproval is disapproval whichever way you look at it.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer reads the same forwards and backwards, which is the whole wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An interjection expressing mild disapproval or annoyance.

clue.text: Talk about having holes in trousers!

indicators.note: talk about says the word is spoken, so we want something that sounds like it

parts.note: breaches are holes or gaps

explanation.surface: An exclamation about holes worn through someone's trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' and 'in' are links; BREACHES and the answer are pronounced alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: short trousers fastened below the knee, an old-fashioned word for trousers.

clue.text: Plant last four with the ultimate in style

parts.note: the end is the last part
IV is four in Roman numerals

indicators.note: the ultimate in a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A team finishes fourth but does it with great flair.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a leafy salad vegetable related to chicory.

clue.text: Indifference to Monday's left over joint?

explanation.surface: Someone shows little interest in the leftovers from the Sunday roast.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the Sunday roast joint is often eaten cold on Monday; a cold shoulder of lamb is that leftover joint.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for deliberate unfriendliness; it is also literally a chilled cut of meat kept from the previous day.

clue.text: Left terrorists with old money

parts.note: the IRA, the Irish Republican Army, a paramilitary group

explanation.surface: Departed militants made off with some old cash.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the Italian currency before the euro replaced it.

clue.text: Cancel a French party

parts.note: un is the French for a
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: Someone calls off a French celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to reverse or annul an action.

clue.text: A bit backward providing information

indicators.note: backward says the phrase a bit is read from end to start

parts.note: a tad is a small amount, a bit

explanation.surface: A slightly slow person is still a source of facts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' turns A TAD round to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: facts and figures collected for reference or analysis.

clue.text: Turn away, rude — badly brought up!

indicators.note: away, as in turned away, says the letters of turn are shuffled
badly says the letters of rude are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rude child is turned away for having been raised poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away' rearranges TURN into NURT and 'badly' turns RUDE into URED.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: reared or raised, cared for while growing.

clue.text: To be more important than being on tour?

parts.note: being on something is being over it, placed on top
a ride is a journey or trip, as a tour is

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether touring matters more than anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the loose reading: being OVER a RIDE is being on a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to take precedence over or prevail against something.
